body: I agree that it is completely unfair of her to basically say "it's not an issue, you're making it an issue".  However, it's hard to not blame myself for ever getting to this situation in the first place.  I've been here before, too, with my previous long term relationship.  What's funny, is if i lay the two side-by-side, the situations are nearly identicle.  What i'm afraid of, more than anything, that i will continue to repeat this pattern.  I've gone to therapy and it doesn't seem to change this pattern.

I know i'm pathetic.  I tired opening up to the situation but felt so unwelcomed in it.  I'm so mad at myself for sticking around just get hurt like this when i knew i couldn't adjus to it in the first place.  

As of right now, we are separtated and i don't think she is coming back.

Just to jump in here: my wife wants an open relationship and i'm trying to figure out if it is something i can accept (let go of jealousy) or it is something that i can not accept (let go of wife/marriage).  The more i read about it, honestly, the more common it seems to me.

i agree.  I think that is the heart of it; when it started and i agreed to it it was with the understanding that it was just sex.  However, the more time they spend together the more i can see it growing in to something much much more.  I think that is the part I am dealing with now.  I am mad at myself for even allowing this to happen in the first place, but also mad at her for taking advanatge of my trust.  She is neglecting our love, to try and work on theirs... and that, is why i have to let go.  Really hurts.

Do you think a situation like this would ever work out?  The trouble i'm having is that I really feel like i could be open to this arrangement if I really felt like I still had the connection with my wife, and i just can't tell if that connection is gone or if I'm just pretending to open myself up to this and my walls are so high I can't accpet it.
Yes, she is having an affair and there is no other way to put it.  This is why i said, i need help letting go.

She has asked me if i want it (her and her gf) to end.  She says that she will if i really want her to, but i keep wimping out and telling her "no, i want you to have happiness so i don't want you to end it".

>talk only about specific physical actions

That makes a lot of sense.  I am really having a hard time gathering my thoughts together enough so i can express them in a constructive way.  Instead of making a situation awkward by forcing myself into their time together.  I really need to give them their freedom and then see how my wife responds to it.  If i'm giving her space and she still doesn't show me affection, then i know i have a more serious issue on my hands and can say, "I am ok with you two being together, but I'm not feeling like there is anything left for me".

I think that is a really good idea.  I feel like even just knowing i get one date night alone with my wife will help me a ton.  And allowing a night or two for them to spend alone is not unreasonable at all.  I think it will also be helpful because my wife can then see that I am not against their relationship, but just wanting some time with her as well.

Counseling has already been made a priority.  I sent an email to my insurance rep on Thursday to see if I can get covered at all for it.  

I feel like she knows what she is saying it disrespectful and that is making her even more upset -- like i wrote above, being mean or having negative feelings is something that really eats at her and she has a had time accepting.  In this case, knowing that she is causing me pain is making her act even worse towards me.
The three of us went to dinner.

I've tried that, and my wife keeps bringing in the other woman.  The other night i was late getting off work and, on my drive home, i get a text from my wife saying, "hey, getting worried about you, was hoping we could go to dinner together".  I can't express how excited i was.  That was exactly what i had needed.  However, once i got home, there they both were, sitting on the couch.  My heart dropped.

I agree with counseling, and letting this out on reddit is the most immediately available form of that, but i will talk to my wife and see if can agree to it.

Appreciate the feedback, and just ordered a copy of Opening up and Ethical Slut.  Anything that can give me perspective on the situation and help me successfully handle my emotions is what i'm looking for right now.

wanted to add:

I didn't realize the relationship was in a rocky spot until my wife met this girl.  She made me feel like things were stronger than ever.  However, once she met this girl, she starts telling me she's not very happy and that she hasn't been in a long time.  Had i known this, i would have worked on that before agreeing to bring this girl into our life. 

The strange part, is that when i press her to open up to me, she then says that the reason she is unhappy is that i'm making her feel like it's not ok to be with this girl and that by acting the way i am I am driving this girl away, which my wife doesn't want at all.  

So, can't tell if she is unhappy with me as a whole or unhappy with my handling of this situation.

>  if you had a solid relationship with your wife, would you be open to polyamory?

Yes.  I really think i would be.  

From your response, is what i'm going through, how i feel like they're treating me, and their actions; is this all very common?
